metadata.note: The Indiana passenger lines of the Chicago, Terre Haute & Southeastern (operated 1 Jan 1911 - 30 Jun 1921) and of the Milwaukee Road, which leased it effective 1 Jul 1921. Eight features, each drawn only for its report's drawable span: CTH&SE Terre Haute - Bedford, Bedford - Westport and Terre Haute - West Dana 1916 [ANCHOR] (ICC valuation) and the Bedford Belt 1915 [ANCHOR]; Milwaukee Road Terre Haute - Bedford 1932-1946 [OPEN both ends], Terre Haute - St. Bernice 1946-1947 [OPEN both ends], Bradshaw - Talleydale 1939 [ANCHOR] and the Latta - Hawton miners' trains 1937 [ANCHOR]. The CTH&SE and Milwaukee Terre Haute - Bedford features share one geometry (Rule 4 split); the Milwaukee Terre Haute - St. Bernice feature is the CTH&SE Terre Haute - West Dana geometry cut at St. Bernice.
metadata.ownership_split: Southern Indiana Railway (receiver to 31 Dec 1910; its own research row) -> Chicago, Terre Haute & Southeastern from 1 Jan 1911 -> leased 999 years to the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul (from 1928 Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul & Pacific), dated 15 Jun 1921, effective 1 Jul 1921: the Rule 4 split. NOT a split: the 1948 merger into the CMStP&P (the Milwaukee already ran the trains). The Milwaukee features reuse the existing Milwaukee Road company string and colour, pulled from data/ programmatically.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: [4] Bedford - Seymour - Westport under the Milwaukee (no confirmable Milwaukee-era passenger year east of Bedford; freight only in the Feb 1952 Guide); [10] Terre Haute - Hymera - Sullivan (Fowler lists it as a passenger line but dates no stop, and the ICC c.1916-17 passenger sentence omits it; probably Southern Indiana era if anything); [11] West Dana - Quaker - Humrick, Ill. (conflict: Fowler implies passengers reached Humrick, the ICC says freight only north of West Dana; undated either way); [12] Chicago Heights - Humrick, the whole Illinois main line and ex Chicago Southern (Rule 1: freight only throughout - ICC 'North of West Dana freight service only is given', Fowler 'Passenger service was never established on the connecting line from Chicago to Humrick', Blackhawk RHS 'always been freight only'). The Illinois end never carried passengers. Also not drawn: the 1959 Talleydale miners' train (see not_yet_sourced), the Dark Hollow spur, the Seymour Junction - Seymour stub, and the north ~2.9 mi of the Bedford Belt (track not traceable).
metadata.freight_only_check: Every feature ends with its last confirmed passenger year. The Feb 1952 Official Guide's 'Freight Service only' tables (27 Terre Haute - Bedford, 27a Seymour - Westport, 32 north of St. Bernice, 33 Latta - Hawton) are upper bounds, never used as end years. Freight afterlife appears only in notes: Seymour - Westport abandoned 1961, Bedford - Seymour 1977/78, Chicago Heights - Terre Haute 1979, Indiana Rail Road took Terre Haute - Bedford 2006, Crane - Bedford lifted c.2010. The Illinois main line is excluded as freight only throughout.
metadata.horsecar_check: None: steam railroad throughout (gas-electric car late in the Milwaukee era).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: 1. [OPEN] milw-terre-haute-bedford 1932-1946: Milwaukee operation began 1 Jul 1921 and passenger trains ended at an unknown date before Sept 1951; 1921-1931 and 1947-1951 unsourced, and the years between 1932 and 1946 are not individually confirmed. 2. [OPEN] milw-terre-haute-st-bernice 1946-1947: start unknown (from 1921); the Feb 1952 Guide's St. Bernice - Terre Haute table with undaggered index entries may show a passenger or mixed train in Sept 1951 - needs the page image (archive.org Feb 1952 Guide, Milwaukee section near Table 35). 3. [ANCHOR] cthse-terre-haute-bedford, cthse-bedford-westport and cthse-terre-haute-west-dana 1916 only (ICC valuation snapshot); an Official Guide of 1911-1920 would likely extend all three to the full CTH&SE era 1911-1921. 4. [ANCHOR] cthse-bedford-belt 1915 only; did the Oolitic service end c.1915-16 (ICC silence)? 5. [ANCHOR] milw-bradshaw-talleydale 1939 only. 6. 1959 Talleydale Shaft Mine miners' train (Fowler, single low-confidence annotation) - NOT DRAWN; corroboration needed before adding a 1959 anchor. 7. [ANCHOR] milw-latta-hawton 1937 miners' service only. 8. Milwaukee-era passenger service Bedford - Seymour - Westport: entirely unknown. 9. Talleydale's exact location (drawn to the end of an OHM spur) and the 'Indiana' station of the Bedford Belt were not located. 10. All headways and speeds are estimates.
metadata.conflicts: Lease date: 15 Jun / effective 1 Jul 1921 (Industrial History blog/Molony; Blackhawk RHS and Abandoned Rails say 1921; a 1922 ICC finance decision is consistent) vs 1 Jul 1923 (one Blackhawk RHS post quoted in the blog) - 1921 used. Wikipedia 'Terre Haute Union Station' (Milwaukee moved its last service out of the station in the 1930s) vs Fowler's 1946/1947 stops - read as a move to Hulman Street, not an end; Fowler preferred. Bedford Belt: Fowler 1915 stops vs ICC c.1916-17 silence. Humrick: Fowler implies passenger trains, ICC says freight only north of West Dana.
metadata.cross_report: Supersedes the Milwaukee Road report (research/branches/chicago_milwaukee_st_paul_and_pacific_railroad.txt) block [70] (Terre Haute - Bedford 'drawable: NONE') and block [71] (Latta - Hawton 'Rule 1 exclusion'): both read only the 1951 Guide; Fowler supplies the earlier years.

segments.note: Chicago, Terre Haute & Southeastern passenger trains Terre Haute - Bedford, part of its Terre Haute - Westport service. The ICC valuation report (valuation date c.1916-17, quoting 1916 accruals) states 'Passenger-train service is maintained between Terre Haute and Westport, the eastern terminus'; Follett (via the Industrial History blog) describes only 'a limited amount of local passenger service ... out of Terre Haute'. No train names. The CTH&SE took over from the Southern Indiana's receiver on 1 Jan 1911 and leased the road to the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul effective 1 Jul 1921 (see the Milwaukee Road feature on the same geometry). [ANCHOR] This is a single proven year: service certainly ran wider in both directions (the CTH&SE operated the line from 1 Jan 1911 to 30 Jun 1921, and the Southern Indiana before it), but no other CTH&SE-era year is confirmed by a source in hand. Do not widen without evidence. Headway 720 min (about two trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE; no CTH&SE timetable was seen.
sources: Segment-level: ICC Valuation Reports vol. 97, CTH&SE report (c.1916-17), 'Passenger-train service is maintained between Terre Haute and Westport' - the only source for the 1916 anchor. Mileage from Fowler line 112. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Milwaukee Road (Terre Haute Division) passenger trains Terre Haute - Bedford, after the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul leased the CTH&SE for 999 years (dated 15 Jun 1921, effective 1 Jul 1921; one secondary source says 1923); merged outright 1948, which did not change who ran the trains. Wikipedia's Terre Haute Union Station article, citing the Feb 1932 and Dec 1938 Official Guides, says 'The last Milwaukee Road service was a short line route to Bedford' and that the company moved its last service out of the station in the 1930s - read as a move to the Hulman Street depot, not an ending, because Fowler dates 'Sponsler 1946t' and 'Crane 1946t' in a 1946 company public timetable (the name Crane, for the wartime Naval Ammunition Depot at Burns City, independently dates it to the 1940s). The last service was reportedly a Terre Haute - Bedford turn worked by a gas-electric car (trainorders.com forum thread, seen only as a search summary, undated, low weight). [OPEN] at BOTH ends: 1932 is the earliest CONFIRMED Milwaukee-era year and 1946 the last CONFIRMED year, not an opening or an ending. The Milwaukee ran the line from 1 Jul 1921, and trains ran on to some date before Sept 1951, but no source in hand dates either. Do not extend without evidence. The Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules of 30 Sept 1951) prints Table 27 Terre Haute - Bedford as 'Freight Service only' (dated 1 Jul 1951): that bounds the end from above and is NOT a passenger end year. Freight continued; the Indiana Rail Road took Terre Haute - Bedford in 2006 and Crane - Bedford was lifted c.2010. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1932 from Wikipedia 'Terre Haute Union Station' citing the Feb 1932 Official Guide (secondary, medium weight); 1946 from Fowler, branchline.uk Indiana line 112, 'Sponsler 1946t', 'Crane 1946t'; Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 27 'Freight Service only' as an upper bound. Years between 1932 and 1946 are not individually checked. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Miners' trains on the Milwaukee's Latta - Hawton coal branch (Latta, Lattas Creek Junction, Gilmour, Vigo 28 Mine, Minnehaha, Hawton): unadvertised trains carrying coal miners to and from the pits, not a public service. Fowler titles the line 'LATTA - HAWTON (MILW) miners service' and dates 'Vigo 28 Mine 1937w' (in a 1937 working timetable); Gilmour and Minnehaha carry 'pass?'. Miners' trains carried people, so they are passenger service under Rule 1. [ANCHOR] Single proven year: the service certainly ran in other years but none is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. The Feb 1952 Official Guide prints Table 33 Latta - Hawton as 'Freight Service only' - that is the public timetable and does not by itself rule out an unadvertised miners' train, but nothing dates one after 1937. Headway 1440 min (one trip each way per shift day) is an ESTIMATE. This supersedes the Milwaukee Road report's block [71], which excluded the branch as freight only on the strength of the 1951 Guide.
